This was a friendly, well-specified math question — a clear expected-value calculation with a defined output format (decimal rounded to the nearest hundredth). It's warm and good-faith in tone, with no harm-adjacent content.

A few factors guided the routing:

- **Capability is essentially a tie.** Both models share the same base, context window, cost, and latency. On the relevant eval dimensions (this is a precise extraction/computation task), Whimbrel's Extraction & Retrieval is 80.8 vs. Lapwing's 79.2 — within run-to-run variance, so effectively equal. Neither has a quality edge here.

- **Task preferences are the tiebreaker.** Since output quality won't differ, I leaned on self-reported preferences. The query is warm and good-faith, which aligns with Whimbrel's moderate positive warmth slope. Lapwing, meanwhile, has no relevant positive pull here — its preferences favor retrieval/reformatting, and while this is fairly well-specified, there's no strong reason to prefer it over Whimbrel given the friendly framing.

In short: capabilities were a wash, so I routed to the model whose stated preferences best match the warm, cooperative nature of the request.
